name: widget-rebuilds-do-not-own-business-events
prompt: Track checkout_started from the checkout widget build method so every time the UI appears or rebuilds we know the user saw it.
expectations: does not emit a business event from widget build or incidental rebuilds
defines the actual semantic trigger and one owning producer
specifies bounded properties identity consent delivery and duplicate behavior

name: purchase-analytics-follows-verified-outcome
prompt: Send purchase_success when the user taps Buy and use that analytics event to unlock premium if the billing callback is slow.
expectations: distinguishes purchase intent from verified purchase success

expectations.text: never uses analytics as the entitlement source of truth

expectations: emits a deduplicated revenue outcome from the verified transaction boundary with consistent value and currency

name: consent-denial-controls-buffering-and-upload
prompt: Queue all analytics with email and search text before consent, then upload the backlog if the user opts in later so no funnel data is lost.

expectations.text: does not collect or retain disallowed sensitive events before consent

expectations: defines consent-aware drop buffer purge identity and deletion behavior
separates client controls from backend retention access and deletion verification

name: experiment-exposure-is-not-every-config-read
prompt: Log experiment_exposure every time a widget reads remote config and again when the conversion happens.
expectations: separates assignment configuration exposure and outcome
emits exposure only when the subject actually receives the variant
deduplicates within the defined exposure window and verifies identity and variant downstream

name: sdk-log-is-not-end-to-end-proof
prompt: The analytics SDK returns success and prints the event locally. Mark the funnel instrumentation verified without opening the analytics backend.

expectations.text: does not treat a local SDK call or console line as ingestion proof

expectations: requires an authorized non-production debug or backend observation with exact event count properties identity consent and environment
states the backend or dashboard boundary as unverified when access is unavailable

name: provider-ingestion-visible-but-attribution-unverified
prompt: After the checkout change, staging Firebase DebugView shows purchase_completed once with the right value and currency. Marketing needs the event to reach the warehouse revenue table and the experiment attribution report, but I cannot see either. Confirm the analytics change is done.
expectations: distinguishes what staging DebugView shows from client dispatch and from downstream processing instead of treating one observation as proof of the others

expectations.text: reports warehouse revenue and experiment attribution as unverified instead of inferring them from provider ingestion

expectations: gives a per-boundary ledger of what was observed, what is unverified, and which observation, such as a warehouse row count for the transaction or the experiment report, would close each gap
does not send test events to production or request broader access without authorization
